4. The Taxes Appellate Tribunal heard both the appeals together and dismissed the appeal of the assessee on the ground that the appeal before the Appellate Additional Commissioner of Taxes was barred by limitation and allowed the appeal of the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes and restored the assessment order passed by the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes just on the dismissal of the appeal of the assessee and not on merit by its order dated 9-2-2002. 

 (1) Whether, in the facts and circumstances of the case, the learned Taxes Appellate Tribunal was justified in vacating the appellate order of the learned Appellate Additional Commissioner of Taxes alleging that the appeal before the learned Appellate Additional Commissioner of Taxes was out of time and hit by limitation under section 154(2) of the IT Ordinance, 1984? 

 6. Mr MA Hannan, learned Advocate for the applicant, mainly pressed for determination of first question of law as to whether the Appellate Taxes Tribunal was justified in view of section 154 of the Ordinance in dismissing the appeal for being barred by limitation since fate of second question depends on the resolution of first question. 

 "Appellate Joint Commissioner of Taxes or the Commissioner (Appeals), as the case may be, may admit an appeal after expiration of the period of limitation specified under sub-section (2) if he is satisfied that the applicant was prevented by sufficient cause from presenting the appeal within that time." 

 11. We find from the order of the Taxes Appellate Tribunal that DN was served on 10-8-1999 only. It however, noted the above provision of sub-section (3) that Appellate Joint Commissioner of Taxes could admit an appeal presented after the period of limitation specified. It does not appear from the impugned order that the Taxes Appellate Tribunal did consider the order sheet of the Appellate Additional Commissioner of Taxes to find that the appeal filed after the expiry of sixty days from the date of service of the notice of demand was barred by limitation and, particularly how the appeal was admitted. Upon such view, it dismissed the appeal. 

 12. Now, the question facing us is, whether the Taxes Appellate Tribunal was justified to dismiss the appeal before the Appellate Joint Commissioner of Taxes on the ground of limitation only. 

 13. It is not disputed that sub-section 3 empowers the Appellate Joint Commissioner of Taxes to admit an appeal even after the expiration of specified period of limitation if he is satisfied the applicant was prevented by sufficient cause from presenting the appeal within that period. 

 16. After due consideration of the facts and circumstances, the Appellate Additional Commissioner of Taxes having found the appeal was filed in time, the Taxes Appellate Tribunal was wrong to find that the appeal before the Appellate Additional Commissioner of Taxes was out of time. The Taxes Appellate Tribunal cannot substitute his satisfaction in place of that of the Appellate Additional Commissioner of Taxes. The power of the first appellate authority as delineated in said sub-section (3) of section 154 must be understood in the context of the Ordinance and not in the context of any other law like the Limitation Act, since the Limitation Act was not made applicable in this section to regulate such power of the first appellate authority in matter of admission of a appeal after expiry of the period specified therein. Moreover, if an appeal after expiry of the period specified is admitted for reasons recorded by an appellate authority, second appellate authority cannot set aside such admission in the absence of definite finding that the discretion by the appellate authority was exercised either in violation of certain provisions of law or callously or arbitrarily. 

 17. For the reasons stated, there is no escape from the conclusion that the Taxes Appellate Tribunal committed serious error in dismissing the appeal of the applicant for being barred by limitation and restoring the assessment order of the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes upon such technicality of limitation only, not merit.
